guides.title: Claude
guides.verdict: Use it for anything that needs to be read carefully and thought through. Do not treat it as the final word.
guides.bestFor: Long documents, complex drafts, work that has to hold its context, and code.
guides.carefulWith: Facts, numbers, and anything going out under your name without a check.
guides.whatIdDo: Start free. Pay for Pro the week the limits start costing you real time.
guides.figCaption: Where Claude carries the work, and where you still have to.

guides.title: ChatGPT
guides.verdict: The generalist. It will have a go at anything, which is exactly why you have to check it.
guides.bestFor: First drafts, thinking out loud, images, and a bit of everything else.
guides.carefulWith: Anything where roughly right is not good enough.
guides.whatIdDo: If you are only ever going to pay for one, pay for this one.
guides.figCaption: What ChatGPT does well, and the jobs I would not hand it.

guides.title: Gemini
guides.verdict: The one that already has your calendar, your Drive and your inbox. That is the whole argument for it.
guides.bestFor: Teams already living in Google Workspace, and research across your own files.
guides.carefulWith: Opening up your whole Drive before you have checked what it can see.
guides.whatIdDo: If your business runs on Google, start here. If it does not, skip it.
guides.figCaption: Gemini earns its place through access, not through cleverness.

guides.title: Copilot
guides.verdict: The one that lives inside Word, Excel and Outlook. Buy it for where it sits, not for how clever it is.
guides.bestFor: Teams already paying for Microsoft 365, especially in Excel and Outlook.
guides.carefulWith: The price. Thirty dollars per person per month adds up fast on a small team.
guides.whatIdDo: Trial it on the five people who live in Excel and Outlook. Not the whole company.
guides.figCaption: Copilot is bought for its address, not its intelligence.

guides.title: Grok
guides.verdict: Fast, loud, and wired into X. Good for watching a story break. Not for work you will put your name on.
guides.bestFor: Real-time chatter on X, plus image and video generation.
guides.carefulWith: Tone and accuracy. It is built to be provocative, and it succeeds.
guides.whatIdDo: Stay on the free tier unless you genuinely work in real-time news.
guides.figCaption: Grok trades caution for speed. Know which one you needed.

guides.title: Mistral
guides.verdict: The European one. Pick it when where your data sits matters more than raw capability.
guides.bestFor: Multilingual work, privacy-sensitive teams, and EU data rules.
guides.carefulWith: A thinner integration ecosystem than the big three.
guides.whatIdDo: Worth the fifteen dollars if data location is a real constraint for you.
guides.figCaption: Mistral wins on where it runs, not on what it can do.

guides.title: DeepSeek
guides.verdict: Very good, very cheap, and hosted in China. That last part is the whole decision.
guides.bestFor: High-volume API work where cost decides it, and coding.
guides.carefulWith: Anything client-confidential on the hosted version.
guides.whatIdDo: Run the open weights on your own hardware, or leave it alone.
guides.figCaption: The capability is not the question here. The hosting is.

guides.title: Kimi
guides.verdict: A serious coding tool at a fraction of the price, with the same hosting question as DeepSeek.
guides.bestFor: Long coding sessions, and turning a prompt into slides or a site.
guides.carefulWith: The same data question, and paid tiers that climb quickly.
guides.whatIdDo: Try it free. Only pay if you are writing code most days.
guides.figCaption: Kimi is cheap where it counts and expensive where it climbs.

guides.title: Meta AI
guides.verdict: Free, already inside WhatsApp and Instagram, and you are the product.
guides.bestFor: Quick answers and quick images in the apps you already have open.
guides.carefulWith: Anything about your business, your numbers or your customers.
guides.whatIdDo: Fine for personal use. Keep your business out of it.
guides.figCaption: Free is the offer. Your data is the price.

guides.title: Manus
guides.verdict: It takes the job, goes away, and comes back with it finished. Impressive, expensive, and it will surprise you.
guides.bestFor: Multi-step research and admin you would otherwise pay someone to do.
guides.carefulWith: Credits, and anything with a login or a payment attached to it.
guides.whatIdDo: Buy one month, give it three real jobs, then decide.
guides.figCaption: An agent is a contractor, not a colleague. Brief it like one.

guides.title: What AI actually is
guides.verdict: It is pattern-matching at enormous scale. Once you see that, most of the hype stops working on you.
guides.bestFor: Anyone who nods along in meetings and would rather not.
guides.carefulWith: Assuming it understands anything. It does not.
guides.whatIdDo: Read this once, then never feel behind in an AI conversation again.
guides.figCaption: Prediction, not understanding. The whole thing in one picture.

guides.title: What a prompt actually is
guides.verdict: A prompt is a brief. If you would not send it to a new hire, do not send it to a model.
guides.bestFor: Getting a usable answer on the first try instead of the fifth.
guides.carefulWith: One-line questions. They get you one-line thinking.
guides.whatIdDo: Steal the four-part brief in this guide and stop starting from scratch.
guides.figCaption: The four things every brief needs, whoever is doing the work.

guides.title: What agentic actually means
guides.verdict: Agentic means it takes actions instead of just answering. That is the whole idea, and the whole risk.
guides.bestFor: Understanding what you are buying when a tool says agent.
guides.carefulWith: Giving something permission before you have watched it work.
guides.whatIdDo: Let it draft. Do not let it send. Not until you have watched it for a fortnight.
guides.figCaption: Answering versus acting. The line where the risk changes.

guides.title: ChatGPT and AI are not the same thing
guides.h1: ChatGPT and AI are not the same thing
guides.verdict: Six words get used as if they mean one thing. They do not, and the difference costs money.
guides.bestFor: Following a sales pitch and knowing which bit is real.
guides.carefulWith: Buying a model when what you needed was a workflow.
guides.whatIdDo: Learn these six words. They are the difference between buying well and buying twice.
guides.figCaption: Six words, sorted, so a sales deck stops working on you.

guides.title: The AI words they keep using
guides.h1: The AI words they keep using
guides.verdict: Most AI jargon is one ordinary idea wearing a lab coat. Here they are, in plain English.
guides.bestFor: Sitting in a meeting and knowing exactly what is being said.
guides.carefulWith: Nodding. Nodding is how you end up on the wrong project.
guides.whatIdDo: Keep this open in a tab for a fortnight. After that you will not need it.
guides.figCaption: The words that come up most, and what each one really means.

guides.title: The three-tool stack I actually use
guides.h1: The three-tool stack I actually use
guides.verdict: Three tools cover almost everything. Everyone selling you a fourth is selling you a fourth.
guides.bestFor: Anyone with eleven browser tabs open and nothing finished.
guides.carefulWith: Collecting tools instead of finishing workflows.
guides.whatIdDo: Pick three. Give each one a job. Cancel the rest this week.
guides.figCaption: Three tools, three jobs, no overlap.

guides.title: The lead follow-up that runs itself
guides.h1: The lead follow-up that runs itself
guides.verdict: Most leads are lost to silence, not to competitors. This fixes the silence.
guides.bestFor: Any business where enquiries arrive faster than you can answer them.
guides.carefulWith: Automating a reply that reads like it came from a robot.
guides.whatIdDo: Build the first two steps this afternoon. Leave the rest until they earn it.
guides.figCaption: Where leads go quiet, and the two steps that stop it.

guides.title: Hire your first AI employee
guides.verdict: Treat it like a hire, not a tool. Job description, trial period, review. That is the whole method.
guides.bestFor: The first task you would happily hand to a junior and never see again.
guides.carefulWith: Hiring it for a job you cannot describe in writing.
guides.whatIdDo: Write the job description first. If you cannot, that is your answer.
guides.figCaption: The same four steps you would use to hire a person.

guides.title: One summary a day: the inbox manager
guides.h1: One summary a day: the inbox manager
guides.verdict: Stop reading your inbox. Read one summary of it, once a day, and act on four lines.
guides.bestFor: Anyone who opens their inbox to check one thing and loses an hour.
guides.carefulWith: Letting it reply on your behalf before you trust its judgement.
guides.whatIdDo: Set it to summarise only. Add sending later, or never.
guides.figCaption: One pass a day, four decisions, inbox closed.

guides.title: Run a business around the clock without working around the clock
guides.h1: Run a business around the clock without working around the clock
guides.verdict: The point is not to work more hours. It is to have the business answer while you are asleep.
guides.bestFor: Solo operators and small teams losing work to time zones and evenings.
guides.carefulWith: Automating a promise you cannot keep the next morning.
guides.whatIdDo: Start with the after-hours reply. It is the one that pays for itself first.
guides.figCaption: What runs while you sleep, and what still waits for you.
